en: Udāna 5.1 Piyatarasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time King Pasenadi of Kosala had gone up to the upper terrace of his excellent palace together with Queen Mallikā.
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to Queen Mallikā:
“Mallikā, is there anyone else who is dearer to you than yourself?
“There is no one else, Great King, who is dearer to me than myself.
But as for you, Great King, is there anyone else who is dearer to you than yourself?”
“Indeed, Mallikā, there is no one dearer to me than myself.
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala descended from his palace and approached the Blessed One.
Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala—
He said this to the Blessed One:
“Here, Bhante, having gone to the upper terrace of the palace together with Queen Mallikā, I said to Queen Mallikā:
‘Mallikā, is there anyone else dearer to you than yourself?’”
When this was said, Queen Mallikā spoke to me thus:
“Great King, there is no one else dearer to me than myself.
But as for you, Great King, is there anyone else dearer to you than yourself?”
When this was said, venerable sir, I said to Queen Mallikā:
“Mallikā, for me too there is no one dearer than myself.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the significance of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Having wandered through all directions with my mind,
I found nothing anywhere dearer than myself; even so,
each person holds their own self dear.”
Therefore, one who desires their own welfare should not harm another. Thus ends the first [verse].
